text:
incident-bot: ALERT: increased rate of serving runtime errors: multiple pods reporting CUDA illegal memory access / invalid device address on pool=gke-infer, start=2026-03-15T10:12:30Z :rotating_light:

maya: I'm on it, paging devon/samir. Observed p50 ok, p99 latency +2s and 5% error rate on /v1/generate. Rolling logs now.

devon: seeing the same. We rolled model inference:v2.3.4 ~10:03 UTC (gradual rollout). Rolling back candidate?

samir: posting tail of dmesg from node gke-infer-14 where pods restarted twice: 
```
[Mar 15 10:11:42] NVRM: Xid (201) 0x43d6 at 0x7f8c2c0000 0x00000000
[Mar 15 10:11:43] nvidia: invalid device address 0x7fffdc123456 in channel 3
[Mar 15 10:11:43] infer_runtime: CUDA illegal memory access at infer_core.cu:214
```

maya: ok cordon gke-infer-14 and drain the pods. ops-sre can you coordinate node actions?

ops-sre: cordoning node gke-infer-14 now (kubectl cordon). Starting drain: `kubectl drain gke-infer-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will keep 2 min for graceful shutdown, then evict.

anna: customer-impact: saw 3 customers hit intermittent 504/500s between 10:12-10:22 UTC (hosted). Incidents page shows spike in token failures. Notifying affected accounts.

devon: quick mitigation: revert inference:v2.3.4 to inference:v2.3.3 on the rollout manager and route 100% back, enable canary at 5% when stable. I'll submit rollback immediately.

maya: please capture core dumps and full container logs before pods die. Use `kubectl logs -p` and grab /var/log/nvidia-installer and dmesg.

samir: grabbing coredump now. Command I'm running on node: `sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "10 minutes ago" > /tmp/kubelet-tail.log` and `sudo gdb --batch -ex "bt" /opt/infer/bin/infer /var/crash/core.* > /tmp/infer-backtrace.txt`

ops-sre: drain finished, pods evicted. Re-scheduling avoided onto same node (taint added). Node will be left cordoned pending postmortem.

devon: rollback submitted at 10:18 UTC — deployment manager shows all replicas back to v2.3.3 by 10:24 UTC. Monitoring metrics.

maya: metrics/observability update: error rate falling (from 5% to 0.9% in 6 min). p99 latency trending down. Still watching for residual crashes.

samir: adding logs snippet from container before restart: 
```
E [10:11:43] infer_core: KV cache write failed, pointer misaligned, attempted addr=0x7fffdc123456 len=256
E [10:11:43] runtime_cu: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

devon: hypothesis: a model codepath in v2.3.4 hits a race that writes misaligned IO into pinned buffer, triggers invalid device address in driver. Not likely kernel upgrade. No system-level rollout in last 24h.

maya: can we repro in staging with the same traffic replay? devon/samir take lead. If confirmed, revert permanent and block v2.3.4 until fix.

samir: kicking off replay job with recorded traffic from 2026-03-15T09:50-10:10. Will try to reproduce on a staging GPU node.

pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to on-call devon (ack required). PagerDuty: devon -> acked at 10:13:05 UTC.

anna: raising severity: Sev2 (customer-facing errors but majority served). Logging customer outreach: template sent, ops to follow up.

ops-sre: created temporary firewall/taint: node:gke-infer-14:ISSUE_3293141592 to avoid scheduling.

devon: reproduction in staging succeeded at low traffic: same CUDA illegal memory access after ~1200 requests. Captured core/backtrace, opened bug INF-8732 with logs attached, labeled priority-high.

maya: next steps checklist: 
- [devon] patch or revert v2.3.4 (in progress, rollback done)
- [samir] full log bundle + coredump uploaded to S3 (link in ticket)
- [ops-sre] cordoned node investigation and kernel/driver audit
- [maya] customer comms and incident timeline

samir: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-incident-archives/3293141592/{dmesg.txt,infer-backtrace.txt,container-logs.tgz}

devon: for engineering: quick diff shows a change in buffer allocation path for dynamic batching in v2.3.4 — adding tests for alignment and stricter pinned memory assertions.

maya: handing to post-incident for root-cause and follow-up. Owner: devon. Please file postmortem and include timeline, mitigation, and code-level fix plan.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: rollback completed, degraded errors reduced to <1% as of 10:30 UTC. Node gke-infer-14 cordoned; investigation in progress.

ops-sre: recommend leaving node cordoned until kernel/driver + hardware vendor triage completes. If additional nodes show same trace, escalate to vendor.

anna: status to customers: sent initial notice at 10:40 UTC; follow-up scheduled once root cause confirmed.

devon: assigning follow-ups in INF-8732: fix branch, test cases, backport to v2.3.x, release window.

maya: final note: no data exfiltration, logs show application-level memory misuse. Postmortem target publish by 2026-03-19. Reaction/emoji: :thumbsup: if you have nothing to add.

samir: +1, will run hardware diagnostics overnight on affected node.

devon: thanks all, keeping ticket updated with repro and patch plan.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED: transitioning to postmortem channel INF-8732-postmortem for long-form analysis.
